newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia consumer sentiment weakens in Q1 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia consumer sentiment weakens in Q1 - survey.

text.p: Malaysian consumer sentiment softened in the first quarter of 1997 from the first and fourth quarters of 1996, a survey by the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said.

The government-backed think-tank said in a report released on Wednesday that its Index of Consumer Sentiments slipped by 2.3 points from the 129.5 reported in both the fourth and first quarters of last year.
Of the 1,277 households interviewed in peninsular Malaysia, 18 percent said their financial income position had improved in the last six months.
This compares with 21 percent and 24 percent, respectively, in the first and fourth quarters of last year.
But 69 percent of the respondents reported no changes in their income situation compared with half a year ago.
Twenty-five percent of the respondents expect a better income position in the next six months, versus 29 percent and 26 percent reported in the first and fourth quarters of 1996.
A majority of 62 percent were confident of maintaining their current income levels, with eight percent predicting a decline, MIER said.
Fifty-five percent of the respondents expect more job openings in the coming two quarters, down from 57 percent reported in the previous quarter and 60 percent in the first quarter of 1996.
On inflationary expectations, the survey found that 79 percent of the respondents expect general prices to rise in the following six months.
That fell short of the 80 percent mark for the first time since the third quarter of 1995.

On spending patterns, 32 percent of those surveyed said now was a good time to invest in housing and in major consumer durable products, up from 28 percent in the first quarter of 1996 and 30 percent in the fourth quarter.
Ten percent said they intended to purchase a house in the next six months, up from eight percent reported in the preceding quarter but lower than the 12 percent charted in the first quarter of 1996.
